key_insight: Combining greedy EV scheduling with TD3 energy dispatch reduced service delays, energy costs, and carbon emissions in simulated PV-powered charging stations.
engineering_relevance: The approach coordinates limited chargers, solar generation, battery storage, and bidirectional grid exchange to support lower-cost, lower-carbon charging.
method: Use a solver-free greedy heuristic to assign EVs based on reductions in service delay.
Use TD3 reinforcement learning to control battery operation while meeting charging demand.
Account for PV and battery exports through export revenue and carbon credits.
evidence_signal: In year-long simulation case studies, SFGH–TD3 achieved the lowest accumulated service delay, energy cost, and carbon emissions among the evaluated heuristic and multi-agent DRL configurations.
watch_item: Simulation results do not establish real-world robustness to uncertain PV output, EV arrivals, or changing tariffs and carbon-credit rules.
paper_title: Electric Vehicle Scheduling and Carbon-Aware Energy Dispatch for Charging Stations
